notes:
I don't have any notes on Job 22 for you yet, because I wasn't able to read any of the sources.

I tried to open five pages at once: the Enduring Word commentary on Job 22, Gill's and Ellicott's commentaries on StudyLight, Precept Austin's Job 22 page, and the NET Bible notes. My code crashed before I could see whether any of those pages had actually loaded. The tool then cut me off for the rest of this turn, so I couldn't check what came back, search for more, or open the Bible Hub, Catholic, Orthodox or tradition-specific pages.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say and to give a link for every point. I haven't read a single page, so anything I wrote now would come from memory. That breaks your rule against filling gaps, so I've left the notes out completely rather than guess.

If you send another message, I'll start again with these steps:
1. **Traditional reading:** read the verse-by-verse commentaries (Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit and others on Bible Hub and StudyLight).
2. **Protestant differences:** search the Baptist, Methodist, Pentecostal, Reformed and Lutheran sites. The verses most likely to come up are v. 2–3 (whether people can benefit God), v. 21–30 (Eliphaz's call to repent, and whether his advice is good even though he wrongly accuses Job) and v. 30 (whether someone guilty can be rescued because of another person's clean hands).
3. **Other views:** look at the NET Bible notes on hard Hebrew wording (v. 20, 24–25, 29–30), New Advent, Catholic Answers and the OCA, and any criticism of prosperity teaching tied to v. 24–28.

Then I'll write it up verse by verse, with a link after each point.
